stem: A client with acute diarrhea reports bloody stool and asks whether to take OTC loperamide. What should the nurse advise?

options.A: Do not use loperamide for bloody or black stool and seek clinical evaluation.
options.B: Take loperamide because bloody stool is an approved indication.
options.C: Double the labeled dose until the bleeding stops.
options.D: Use loperamide only if the client also develops a rash.

rationale: Current OTC loperamide labeling states not to use the medication when stool is bloody or black. Fever and mucus in the stool are also reasons to consult a doctor before use.
educational_objective: Recognize a labeled situation in which OTC loperamide should not be used.
source_locator: Drug Facts—Do not use if you have bloody or black stool
source_claim_supported: Loperamide should not be used for bloody or black stool.
correction_summary: Reframed the item around the explicit current OTC warning and removed unsupported pathophysiologic claims.
audit_findings: Bloody stool directly triggers the label's do-not-use warning.
Other options contradict the warning or add irrelevant criteria.
Independent second pass found a unique answer.
